st: Put the beans in a large pot with [[4 cups]] water. Bring to a hard boil and boil for 10 minutes, which makes the beans safe to eat.
Turn off the heat, cover, and let the beans stand for 1 hour. Drain and discard the soaking water.
Return the beans to the pot with [[4 cups]] fresh water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer for 1 hour until completely tender. Drain, saving a cup of the liquid.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Tip in the beans and a splash of the saved cooking liquid. Season with salt.
Cook, stirring and lightly mashing some beans, for 10 minutes until the sauce clings to the beans. Serve hot with rice, plantains or ubugali.

ing: about 1 lb each, cleaned and scaled
st: Cut 3 diagonal slashes on each side of the fish. Pat the fish dry.
Mix the lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper and rub it over the fish and inside the cavity.
Marinate the fish in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pat the fish dry again and fry for 5 to 6 minutes per side until the skin is crisp and the flesh flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Move the fish to a plate. Wipe out the pan and add the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Cook the onion rings and chili for 4 minutes until soft and lightly browned.
Spoon the onion and chili over the fish and serve hot with ubugali, rice or fried plantains.

ing: such as dried sardines or anchovies
st: Soak the dried fish in warm water for 15 minutes. Drain, rinse well and pat dry.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the fish for 3 minutes until crisp, then remove it to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Add [[0.5 cup]] water, return the fish to the pan, and simmer gently for 8 minutes. Taste before adding salt, since the fish is already salty.
Serve hot with ubugali or rice.

ing: thawed; cassava leaves must be cooked fully
st: Put the cassava leaves in a pot with [[2 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until completely soft. Never eat cassava leaves undercooked.
Meanwhile, heat the palm oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook for 8 minutes until browned and tender.
Stir the onion and eggplant into the cassava leaves.
Whisk the peanut butter with [[1 cup]] hot water from the pot until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Add the spinach and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil shines on top.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or ubugali.
Bring [[2.5 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot with a pinch of salt.
Mix the cassava flour with the cornmeal in a bowl. Whisk [[1 cup]] of this flour mixture into [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Stir that mixture into the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the remaining flour gradually while stirring hard with a wooden spoon to avoid lumps.
Cook over low heat for 10 minutes, pressing and turning the dough, until it is stiff and pulls away from the pot. Cover for 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a pan, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the spinach. Cook for 4 minutes until wilted, then season with salt.
With wet hands, shape the ubugali into smooth balls and serve with the spinach and a stew or beans.
Put the chicken in a large pot with [[6 cups]] water, the onion, turmeric, cumin and salt.
Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken, cool slightly, and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones.
Add the bulgur to the broth and bring back to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat, and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grain is soft and most of the broth is absorbed.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot and stir well.
Beat with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes to make it thick and creamy, adding a splash of hot water if needed.
Stir in the butter and pepper. Serve hot.
Mix the oil, vinegar, garlic, chili, pepper and salt in a large bowl.
Add the goat and stir to coat. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
Soak the skewers in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
Thread the meat onto the skewers, alternating with pieces of onion and pepper.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high.
Grill the skewers for 12 to 15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until browned and cooked through to at least 145°F (63°C).
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with fries, bananas or bread.
